rgb: This indoor bouldering gym has a broad blue padded floor mat in the foreground, with sloped grey, yellow, and blue climbing walls and coloured holds approximately 4 to 6 metres ahead. Immediately in front of the camera wearer, someone wearing grey sweatpants and a black shirt is lying face-up on the mat; their feet extend to within 1 metre of the wearer (arm's reach), while their head is around 2.5 metres away. They look upward while holding a phone above their face with both hands. On the left of the supine person, two people are seated less than 0.5 metres apart and roughly 2.5 to 3.5 metres from the wearer: one wears a black hoodie and faces away toward the climbing wall, while the other, positioned farther left in a pink top, looks toward the camera wearer and raises two fingers in frame 1, then turns forward toward the wall throughout frames 2–5. On the supine person's right, two people in grey and brown shirts sit next to each other about 2.5 to 3.5 metres away, facing the climbing wall. Additional figures stand or sit 5 to 8 metres away in the background, beside a wooden bench at the far left and near the climbing wall's base on both sides. In frame 2, the wearer's left hand enters the lower foreground within 0.5 metres and partly blocks the supine person's right ankle; the person's lower legs also remain partially cropped by the bottom edge in every frame. Between frames 1 and 3, the viewpoint pans slightly right and tilts upward, exposing more ceiling. In frame 4, a person in black shorts enters at the extreme right edge about 2 metres away, partly hidden by the frame boundary; in frame 5, they remain standing in right-profile on the mat as the left-background bench disappears from view.
depth: The monocular depth visualization shows the climbing-gym mat running without interruption from the camera wearer's foreground to a background bouldering wall about 5 to 8 metres distant, with five people forming a semicircle 1 to 4.5 metres in front of the wearer. At centre foreground, a person in grey trousers lies on their back, their feet 0.8 to 1.2 metres from the wearer and therefore within arm's reach in frame 2, when the wearer's brightly illuminated left hand extends at approximately 0.3 metres and partly obscures the person's right foot. Their head and hands, which hold a phone, are at approximately 2.5 metres. Two seated people in pink and black tops occupy the left, and two in grey and tan tops occupy the right; they are about 0.5 to 1 metre apart and 2.5 to 4.5 metres away. All face away toward the upper wall, and none looks at the camera wearer apart from the pink-shirted person, who glances somewhat sideways in frame 1. Over the five frames, the wearer's view pans slightly left and tilts upward while a person wearing black shorts approaches from the right. They first appear in frame 4 as a bright vertical silhouette at approximately 1.5 metres, partially outside the right edge, then step onto the mat and stand about 2.5 metres away on the right in frame 5, facing away toward the wall and within arm's reach (approximately 1 metre) of the rightmost seated person. Relative to RGB, this depth map immediately clarifies both the continuous ground-plane distance gradient over the blue mat and the strong depth discontinuity separating the approaching standing person from the seated group. Beyond 5 metres, however, it becomes unreliable: the sloping wall, its holds, and distant standing or seated figures 6 to 8 metres away at the far left and near the wall collapse into uniform black, eliminating their geometry.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation visualization separates the group on the mat into individual `person` masks: the centrally positioned supine person 1 to 2.5 metres away, whose feet are clipped by the lower frame boundary in frames 3–5; the two people seated on the left at 2.5 to 3.5 metres, with the black-hoodie wearer partly blocking the pink-shirted person's right side; and the two seated figures on the right at 2.5 to 4 metres, who move from the right border into complete view by frame 4 as the camera pans. The map additionally segments the distant people at far left during frames 1–3—figures standing and sitting on a bench 6 to 8 metres away while facing right—and a standing person at the climbing wall's base, approximately 5 to 6 metres distant and facing the seated group and camera wearer. It also captures the black-shorts wearer entering at the far right from 1.5 to 2.5 metres away in frames 4–5, although the top edge crops their upper torso. Throughout the sequence, it follows the apparent rightward movement of the distant left-side figures until they leave through the left edge after frame 3, while the approaching figure on the right enters the area immediately to the seated pair's right. Compared with RGB, the map more clearly separates overlapping shapes into distinct instances, including the wall-side standing climber behind the person in pink in frames 4–5 and the tightly spaced seated pair on the right. Its class labels and completeness are nevertheless extremely unreliable: it labels the blue mat as a `bed` only in frames 1–2 and then omits it, joins the wearer's foreground hand in frame 2 to the supine person's mask, identifies the supine person's elevated hands and phone as a `banana` in frame 3, and sporadically assigns background wall elements or people the labels `tv`, `dog`, `sports ball`, or `car`.
pose: The pose visualization remains nearly completely empty throughout all five frames, detecting no skeletons for the person lying in front of the camera wearer, the seated group 2.5 to 4.5 metres away, or the standing figure on the right at 1.5 to 2.5 metres. In frame 2, it draws a magenta hand skeleton for the wearer's own left hand, which is raised in the lower-left foreground at approximately 0.3 metres and lies within reach of the supine person's right leg. In frame 4, it represents the supine person's raised hands and phone at approximately 2.5 metres merely as a tiny magenta cluster near the bottom centre. The only person given yellow body keypoints is the rightmost seated individual in the tan shirt, approximately 3.5 to 4 metres away, in frames 3 and 5. This person sits to the right of the grey-shirted individual and faces away toward the climbing wall; the keypoints depict their head, torso, and bent right arm and leg resting on the mat, within approximately 0.5 metres of the grey-shirted person on their left and approximately 1 metre of the standing person on their right. The pose map contributes information beyond RGB by precisely articulating the finger joints of the wearer's egocentric hand in frame 2 and showing the rightmost sitter's limb angles despite their back-facing posture. Overall, though, it is severely unreliable because of extreme false negatives for almost every visible person—probably resulting from supine foreshortening, occlusions involving back-facing bodies, and framing cutoffs—and because the sole detected person's torso keypoints are noisy and collapsed in frames 3 and 5.
